title: "Objectives & prerequisites"

## Learning objectives

::: {.callout-note title="Learning objectives"}
- Run an end-to-end path in which a Crossplane XR is turned into an
  EngineeringTask and a Sandcastle constructs the requested artifact.
- Observe that Crossplane's composition **requests** engineering work
  by declaring an EngineeringTask; it does not write any Pico code.
- Observe that the Sandcastle only sees the EngineeringTask — the XR
  never crosses the compose → construct boundary.
- Confirm that the construction stage is **parametric on the
  request**: change `spec.value` in the XR and the durable branch's
  `rules/hello.yaml` changes to match, without touching any script.
- Confirm that the artifact boundary from
  [Sandcastle · Part 1 · Lesson 1](../../courses/sandcastle/part-1/01-inside-a-sandcastle/index.html)
  still holds: only the branch survives; the sandbox and the task file
  inside it are disposed.
:::

## Prerequisites

::: {.callout-note title="Prerequisites"}
- Completion of the
  [Hello World Pico Sandcastle lab](../hello-world-pico-sandcastle/)
  — this lab reuses the same PATH-allowlist Sandcastle shape, but
  driven by an EngineeringTask instead of a static blueprint.
- Reading familiarity with
  [Crossplane · Part 1](../../courses/crossplane/part-1/01-composing-hello-pico-on-kubernetes/index.html)
  so the `XHelloWorldPico` XR shape is recognisable.
- A working shell (`bash` or `zsh`).
- **`git` 2.30+** and **`python3` 3.8+** on your `PATH`.
- A local clone of this repository, which ships the reference `pico`
  CLI under `bin/pico`.
:::

## Environment

- **Supported OS:** macOS, Linux, or WSL.
- **Required shell:** `bash` 3.2+ or `zsh` 5+.
- **Required tools:**
  - `bash` (POSIX shell) — invoked by the driver and by
    `./build/hello-world-pico`.
  - `git` **2.30+** — seeds the local target repo, commits the branch
    inside the sandbox, and pushes it back.
  - `python3` **3.8+** — used by `compose.sh` to extract fields from
    the XR, by `sandcastle-run.sh` to read the EngineeringTask, and
    by `bin/pico`.
  - `pico` (this repository's reference CLI, shipped under
    `bin/pico`) — parses `rules/*.yaml` and composes the
    `hello-world-pico` artifact.
- **PATH expectation:** after one-time setup, `command -v pico`
  resolves to `<repo>/bin/pico`, not `/usr/bin/pico` (the Alpine/nano
  text editor).
- **Estimated time:** 30–45 minutes.
- **No cluster, container, or network access is required.** The
  entire lab runs against a local target repo under `work/`.

## One-time setup

From a fresh shell, in a local clone of the academy source
repository, put its `bin/` directory on your `PATH`:

```bash
export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"
command -v pico   # should print .../bin/pico
```

The `PATH` export lasts for the current shell session; re-run it in
new shells. This is the same one-time setup used by the
[Hello World Pico Sandcastle lab](../hello-world-pico-sandcastle/objectives.html#one-time-setup).

## Cleanup

The lab writes only inside the repository-ignored `work/` directory.
To remove everything the lab produced:

```bash
rm -rf work/compose-sandcastle-request
```

The `sandcastle-run.sh` driver already deletes its own sandbox
workspace at the end of each run; the command above additionally
removes the seeded local target repo, the emitted EngineeringTask,
and the captured evidence.
